Samatha in practice points toward calm collectedness. This app tries to reward relaxed alertness rather than quiet drowsiness, so the feedback signal fades down when the frontal pattern looks sleepy or contaminated.

The clean baseline calibration lasts 60 seconds. For the first 30 seconds you sit still with your eyes open; for the second 30 seconds you relax your face and close your eyes. Each half sets its own personal median and MAD baselines, and a session is scored against the half that matches its eyes setting (closed or open). During the session the baseline adapts slowly, over a 30-minute window blended with the calibration, so it follows electrode drift without erasing a sustained good state.

After the clean baseline, you can run a short 25-second artefact capture. It records eye movements, jaw clench, and forehead tension so blink and EMG thresholds can be personalised without contaminating the clean meditation baseline.
The live reward is a personalised frontal-state classifier built from 5-second raw EEG windows, updated every second. Dashboard audio uses the source chosen in the Session card.

Drowsiness is estimated first so the app does not confuse sleepy theta-heavy slowing with useful meditation feedback. Its evidence combines TAR, TBR, entropy, and ABR, so a settled state here means relaxed and awake, not merely low-energy.
This is a non-medical training aid built around one dry frontal electrode at FP1 with an ear reference. It cannot infer whole-brain state, connectivity, source localisation, or meditative attainment.
Choose any metric to see the formula, terms, and practical interpretation used by the live model. This section is for educational transparency, not diagnosis.

All computed metrics share a common set of constraints: one dry frontal electrode (FP1), an ear reference, 512 Hz sampling through the MindWave Mobile 2 headset, 5-second analysis windows, and a personal calibration session conducted under the same conditions. Departing from any of these conditions reduces the reliability of all derived metrics equally.
The app includes short offline summaries and optional links for deeper reading.

A practical reward proxy for relaxed, alert, clean settling.
It rises when settledness, alertness, and usable signal quality all stay strong together.

This is the main dashboard reward. It is intentionally conservative: contamination and sleepy slowing fade it down so the app does not reward quiet but unusable or drowsy windows. Settledness and alertness are combined as a geometric mean, so at your baseline it reads about 50% (less any quality penalty) and a high reading needs both to be high together.
This is a reward heuristic for audio feedback and session trends, not a clinical meditation score. Individual calibration quality affects the reading.
How much the current frontal pattern looks calm but still organized.
It rises when alpha-over-beta balance looks more settled without a strong theta-heavy pull toward drowsiness.
Settledness tries to represent relaxed but awake settling. It is not simple slowing, and it is not meant to reward a dull or sleepy state.
Frontal α/β balance is highly state- and person-specific. The score is z-scored against your own session baseline, so its first few minutes are less stable.
Alpha-over-beta ratio. Higher values often look calmer, as long as they are not paired with sleepy slowing.
Theta-over-alpha ratio. Higher values can point toward drowsier slowing, so settledness subtracts some of it.
A proxy for stable regulation versus drifting.
It rises when theta-to-beta balance stays lower than the user\'s baseline.
Control is a compact frontal control proxy. Read it as more or less stable regulation, not as a literal measure of willpower or intelligence.
θ/β regulation patterns overlap with task-demands and mental effort. High control during meditation may reflect active steering more than effortless stability.
Theta-over-beta ratio. Higher values often look more drifty; lower values tend to look more controlled.
The inverse of the drowsiness model.
It falls when theta-heavy slowing rises while entropy and alpha-over-beta balance move in a drowsy direction.

Alertness is a practical wakefulness proxy for this device and montage. It is not a clinical vigilance score, but it is useful as a session feedback source because it cleanly separates awake from sleepy quietness.
Alertness inherits all limits of the drowsiness model. It is not a clinical vigilance measure and can fluctuate with eyes-closed relaxation even when the user is awake.
Frontal slowing evidence that tries to separate sleepy quietness from useful settling.
It rises with higher TAR, higher TBR, lower entropy, and lower ABR. Brief spikes can still happen with eyes-closed slowing or very low-complexity windows.
This is not a sleep-stage detector. On a single dry FP1 electrode it should be read as drowsy-like evidence, not proof that the user is falling asleep.
Drowsy and relaxed patterns are hard to separate at single-electrode FP1 resolution. Brief elevated readings can happen during deep relaxation, not only during drowsiness.
Theta-over-alpha ratio. When this rises, the window looks more slowed and sleepy.
Theta-over-beta ratio. Higher values can indicate reduced control and more drowsy-like drift.
Spectral entropy over 4–30 Hz. Lower entropy means the spectrum is simpler and more repetitive, which often happens in sleepy slowing.
Alpha-over-beta ratio. Higher values can support settledness; lower values in this model count toward drowsiness.
How contaminated the current signal looks.
It rises with poor contact, blink or transient activity, muscle-like high-frequency activity, clipping, and signal gaps (lost samples).
This is the main contamination gate. High artefact means the app should stop trusting the state estimate and reduce reward, even if the waveform also looks quiet.
AS = 0.30 × contact + 0.10 × line + 0.25 × EMG + 0.16 × blink + 0.12 × clip + 0.10 × stall
Sitting very still and ensuring good headset contact reduces this significantly. Jaw clenching, forehead tension, and loose electrodes are the most common sources.
How much the app trusts the current window as usable input.
It rises when artefact score is low.
Quality confidence is the clean-signal complement of artefact score. It does not mean the classification is perfect; it means the window is usable enough to trust more.
High quality confidence means the window passed artefact screening, not that the classification is correct. Correct classification additionally requires a well-established personal baseline.
A proxy for active re-focusing or deliberate correction.
It rises when beta-related control looks stronger while settled alpha-over-beta balance is not dominant.
Effortful focus is not automatically better meditation. It often reflects steering, correction, or task-like control, so it is shown for reference and is not offered as a feedback source.
Effortful focus during meditation is not automatically better practice. It is shown for reference only and is not offered as a feedback source.
A proxy for awake drift, reduced regulation, or loosening attention.
It rises when theta-over-beta increases without the more settled alpha-over-beta pattern, especially when entropy does not support a clean stable state.
This is a lightweight awake-drift proxy for live feedback, not a thought-content detector. It is most useful as a disorganization axis: more wandering usually means more drift and less continuity.
Awake drifting is not reliably separable from settled contemplation at single-electrode FP1. Use this as a loose disorganisation proxy, not as a definitive thought-content indicator.
Theta-over-beta ratio. Higher values often look more drifty or less controlled.
Alpha-over-beta ratio. Stronger settled alpha-over-beta balance pushes mind-wandering evidence back down.
Spectral entropy. In this score it helps distinguish awake, varied activity from simplistic sleepy slowing.
